entries.title: The bank: saving, borrowing, investing
entries.answer: The bank keeps your coin, pays interest and lends. Right-click its desk (open 7:30am to 5:30pm) or ask the banker 'The bank'.
more: Right-click the bank's ledger desk (open 7:30am-5:30pm), or ask the banker 'The bank' (Trade → Money): deposit, withdraw, see your statement, borrow, repay, or take a mortgage.
Your account earns the savers' interest.
Before a town has a bank, its savings club keeps the coin.
steps: Find the bank (a town of thirty in the Iron Age builds one facing the square).
Deposit or withdraw an amount; borrow if you're a friend of the town (up to more as an honoured guest).
Invest… ('I'd like to invest 50 coins') takes a share of what the town takes in for two weeks.
controls: [Right-click] the banker → Trade → Money → The bank · Invest…
tips: The money changer swaps gold for coin at the mint's rate both ways (nine coins a bar).
Short of coin for a business? The bank lends what you're short in the same click.
warn: A debt left a fortnight shames you; three weeks behind on a mortgage and the house goes back to the town.

entries.title: Buying a house
q: how do i buy a house
buy a home in the village
buy the house im standing in
how much does a house cost
is there a house for sale
entries.answer: Stand in an empty house and press U, then Buy the one I'm in. Ask any folk 'Buy a house' to hear what's for sale.
more: Prices follow the housing market: what a house costs to build times the housing index (dearer where homes are short).
steps: Walk into the empty house.
U → Buy the one I'm in (or take a mortgage at the bank: a fifth down).
controls: [U] → Home → What's for sale? · Buy the one I'm in
[Right-click] a folk → Trade → Services → Buy a house
tips: The property office's Market tab lists buildings for sale, households' houses among them.
A house you buy with a household in it keeps them on as your tenants.

entries.title: Mortgages
q: how do i get a mortgage
entries.answer: A mortgage is the bank's loan on a house: you choose the deposit (borrow 60, 75, 80 or 90% of the price), the term (4 to 24 weeks) and the bank sets the rate by your deposit and credit score. Open it from the bank's desk or Your life in town → Mortgage.
more: The rate is a week's interest on what you still owe: about 2.5% at 60% borrowed, up to 4% at 90%; a little less when the bank is flush or your credit is excellent.
The payment may be no more than a third of what you earned a week over the last fortnight (the affordability bar shows it).

Each seventh day the bank takes the payment from your account. Miss one and an arrears letter comes; three behind and the bank takes the house, sells it, and pays you what it fetched over what you owed.
Overpay any time, remortgage to a new term, or port the loan to another house.
controls: [Right-click] the bank desk → Get a mortgage
warn: Three payments behind and the bank takes the house back.
steps: Open the Mortgages page (the bank's desk, or Your life in town → Mortgage).
Choose a house for sale (Show me points the way).
Choose your deposit and term; read the rate, the weekly payment and the affordability bar.
Take this mortgage: it asks once more, then the keys and the deed are yours.

entries.title: Letting a house and collecting rent
q: can i rent out my house
how do i get rent from tenants
entries.answer: Let a house you own and collect its rent: press U, then Collect rent.
more: A house you own can be let to a household that wants a home, at the rent asked; the rent gathers for you.
Let it from the property office's My property tab.
tips: Rents follow the housing market: they rise when homes are scarce.
Sell a house you own outright back to the town at the bank for four fifths of its price (the tenants stay on).

entries.title: Selling, letting or refitting a building
q: how do i sell my house
refit my shop as a bakery
entries.answer: Sell, let or refit what you own from the property office's My property tab. Offers come in each morning.
more: Every building you own is on the town's property register.

Open the property office → My property (or the Sell, Let and Repurpose buttons on your shop and U page): set a price and offers come in each morning (households, firms, the council, other players), standing three days.
Refit a building to a new use, raise a storey or add a wing, each with a quote.
controls: Property office → My property → Sell · Let · Repurpose
tips: A building's worth is its land, what it would cost to build again less wear, and the goodwill of a business in it.
warn: Selling your shop's building closes your shop in it: its till comes to you and its keeper is let go.

entries.title: Land titles, shares and bonds
q: how do i invest in firms
entries.answer: You can buy land titles and shares in the town's firms. Press U, then Everything you can do, then the Capital tab.
more: U → Everything you can do → Capital: buy land titles (plots on the town's register, which earn), collect what your land has earned, and buy or sell shares of the town's firms on the bourse (holders draw the week's profit as a dividend).
Savings, loans and bonds are at the bank's counter.
steps: Press U → Everything you can do → Capital tab.
Land titles: press Buy it beside a plot; 'Collect what my land has earned'.
Shares: choose the firm and how many, then Buy or Sell.
warn: Shares stand last in a bankruptcy: if a firm fails they can be wiped out.

entries.title: Your finances screen
q: how do i see my finances
the coin button in my inventory
entries.answer: Your finances shows what you have, earn, spend and owe. Press E and click the coin beside the crafting area, or press U, then Finances.
more: Your finances shows what you have, earn, spend and owe: Overview (net worth and its trend, coin carried, the week's income, spending and profit, bills due), By town, Balance sheet, Income & spending, Charts, Businesses, Property, Investments, Bills, Ledger and Notices.
steps: Open it from the coin button in your inventory (E), U → Finances, or the finances key (unbound until you set it).
Click a line on the Balance sheet to jump to its page.
controls: Finances key (set it in Options → Controls)
tips: Weekly summary and bill toasts can be switched off on the Notices tab (or in the client config).

entries.title: The builder: a house or premises of your own
q: how do i build a house
entries.answer: The builder shows the town's plan as real lots: pick one (or your own land), pick a design that fits, and see every block of it standing there in the world before you pay.
more: Green lots are free, blue ones are yours. The chosen lot is outlined on the ground with posts at its corners.
The design gallery shows only what fits your lot, with the builders' quote and time.
Step 3 draws the building itself, translucent, where it would stand: red blocks are where something is in the way. Turn it, nudge it, or Walk round it (U brings you back).
Then the cost line by line and a confirm; the Progress tab shows it rising, the blocks still to go up shown faint.
steps: Open the builder (Your life in town → The builder, the property office's Commission tab, or Start a business → Have the town build it).
Click a lot on the map.
Choose a design.
See it standing; turn or nudge it till nothing is red.
Check the cost and order it.
controls: [U] Your life in town → The builder
tips: A bigger plot (bought on the Land page) takes the villa and the manor.
warn: You pay a deposit now, more at half built, and the balance when it stands.

entries.title: Buying land
entries.answer: Land comes in the town's own sizes: a lot, two side by side, a long lot, a whole block, or a smallholding out past the town for a farm. Your life in town → Land.
more: Pick a size and click a green lot on the map: its outline appears on the ground and the price is broken down.
A friend of the town may hold one lot; a citizen up to four, and one smallholding. Players together hold at most 15% of the town's house lots.
Never for sale: what the town has built or queued, its farmland and mine, lots kept for its hall and trades, and the ring kept clear for it to grow into.
Rates come out of your account each week, doubled once the land has stood empty 14 days. The town buys land back at 80%.
steps: Open Land (Your life in town).
Choose a size.
Click a free lot; walk over and look at its outline.
Buy it: posts with lanterns go up at its corners and the deed is in your pack.
tips: Two titles side by side merge into one bigger plot, unless households are waiting for houses.
The deed is the register's copy: use it to see the title.
warn: Empty land pays double rates after 14 days.

entries.title: Premises: shops, workshops, warehouses, offices, stalls
q: where can i rent a shop
let my shop to a villager
entries.answer: The Premises page lists the town's trading buildings nobody uses, each priced by its zone (the square dearest and busiest, the edge cheapest), to lease week by week or buy, in your name or a firm's.
more: Zones: the square ×1.6, the high street ×1.3, a quarter ×1.0, the edge ×0.7, by a smelter's smoke ×0.85. Rent is 1.5% of the value a week times the footfall.
Uses: a warehouse holds more stock, a workshop has benches, an office takes 5% off a firm's running costs.
Let premises to a villager firm for 4, 8 or 12 weeks; its rent comes into your account.
If a firm goes bankrupt, premises held in its name are sold for its creditors; premises you hold yourself stay yours.
steps: Open Premises (Your life in town, or the Town Hall's Money tab).
Lease or buy a listing (Show me points the way).
Set its use on Your premises, or let it to a villager firm.
tips: A market-day pitch costs a third of a week's stall.
warn: Two weeks behind and a villager firm's lease ends.

entries.title: Renting a home
entries.answer: Home → Rent a home lists the town's empty houses and flats and other players' houses to let. Rent one: you wake in its bed, and the rent goes out each morning from your account.
more: Three days' notice either way.
Rent you can't pay goes on your debts; a week behind and the landlord gives notice.
steps: Open Home (Your life in town).
Rent a home tab: choose one (Show me), Rent it.
tips: Renting ticks the first week's "Find a room" step.

entries.title: Debts, credit and bankruptcy
entries.answer: Every debt you owe in a town is on one ledger (Your life in town → Debts): rates, rent, fines, tabs, loans. A late debt climbs a ladder: a reminder, a late fee, a letter of demand, then your wages, the bailiff or the court.
more: Ask for a plan at any rung: so much a week over six weeks, and the ladder stops while you keep to it.
Consolidate: one bank loan pays off two or more debts (a fair credit score needed).
Your credit score rises with debts paid on time and falls with arrears; it sets the bank's rate.
The bailiff walks to your home and takes goods to the value, never your bed, tools, clothes or a few days' food.
Bankruptcy: when you owe more than you have, the official receiver sells what you have, pays creditors in order, and writes off the rest. Fourteen days of restrictions follow.
steps: Open Debts.
Pay, or Ask for a plan.
If it's hopeless, the Bankruptcy tab explains what happens before you declare.
tips: While you're away the ladder runs at half pace.
warn: Bankruptcy can't be undone and stays on your credit score for six weeks.

entries.title: Your will
entries.answer: Your will (the Town Hall's Money tab, the bank's desk, or Your life in town) says who gets your houses, land, premises and savings: your spouse, a child, a resident friend, the town or the poor fund.
more: It is carried out if you retire your character, or under the long-absence rule.
Debts are paid first from the estate; heirs never inherit debts.
Heirs who are players get new deeds.
steps: Open Your will.
Choose an heir for each part.
Sign and have it witnessed.
controls: [U] Your life in town → Your will

entries.title: Bills while you're away
q: what happens when i log off
entries.answer: Rent, rates and the mortgage are paid from your bank account by standing order while you're away, as long as the money lasts. At login, a page says what was paid and what wasn't.
more: A bill your account can't meet goes on your debts; the ladder runs at half pace while you're away.
Away a long time with bills unpaid, your will is carried out; without one, the town takes your property back, pays your debts from it and keeps the rest in your account.
steps: Keep coin in your bank account before you log off.
